families.theNuanceThatMattersMost: This manifest entry holds TWO different money facts with OPPOSITE held-status, and a repair must not collapse them. The § 1203.4a(e) reimbursement — up to $60 county and $60 city — IS established and the packet must state it. The court FILING fee is expressly 'unresolved and county-specific' and is NOT established, so the named clerk must be kept for that one question. A repair that states the $60/$60 as the filing fee, or that publishes a filing figure, would invent a fact.
families.theParticipantHarmIsTwoSided: The packet currently tells a participant that nothing about cost is established. It thereby withholds both halves of a fact that cuts in the participant's favour: that the reimbursement is capped at $60 + $60, that it is subject to an ability-to-pay determination under PC 987.8(g)(2), and — the manifest says this twice, in pay_fee and again in apply_fee_waiver — that inability to pay it does NOT defeat eligibility. A participant who assumed an unaffordable and disqualifying cost could abandon a petition they are entitled to file.

correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.premise: ca-prop64-set's manifest holds an EXPLICIT NO-FEE FINDING.
correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.finding: WRONG as to location and as to character. The manifest's pay_fee records NON-establishment: 'The source review does not state a filing fee for the CR-400 series.' The no-fee answer is real but lives in src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/CA-california.json — feeRules[3] 'Prop 64 marijuana relief $0 Largely automatic' and feeRules[7] 'Automatic relief and Prop 64 cost nothing.' — which all three of this family's census rows name as a requiredSourceId.

correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.premise: Five of the six cannot enter the central visual gate because 38 of their 58 fixture PDFs are untouched Judicial Council forms ENCRYPTED with objects in xref streams that pdf-lib cannot open; that is DF-003.
correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.finding: DF-003 says something else entirely. Its title is 'Seven California families are silently excluded from the visual gate because their fixtures are named per variant'. The mechanism is that generate-raster-queue.mjs enrols a family by looking for fixtures/canonical.pdf and fixtures/boundary.pdf, and these families ship fixtures in per-variant SUBDIRECTORIES, so the generator records 'no canonical PDF, no boundary PDF' — literally true and, in DF-003's own words, 'completely misleading: the PDFs exist.' Encryption is not the mechanism and is nowhere in the finding.
correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.furtherDetail: DF-003 covers all SEVEN California families including ca-851-91-set, not five of six, and measures 63 PDFs across them, not 58. This worker independently counted 42 fixture PDFs across the six briefed families (8/8/2/8/4/12). The encryption is real but is already handled: the West host reads these forms through a pikepdf bridge with an empty user password, and the committed field census records the basis as 'exact official encrypted binaries... readBy: pikepdf 10.12.0 / libqpdf 12.3.2'. It is not an open blocker.
correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.consequence: The brief's instruction 'do not change any fixture naming' happens to be right, but for the wrong reason — fixture naming is the actual substance of DF-003, and DF-003 defers the fix to the queue GENERATOR rather than to the families. A worker acting on the brief's version would have reported a nonexistent encryption blocker.
correctionsToTheBriefsPremises.severity: MEDIUM — no harm done here, but the premise is not in the record

forTheCaptain.issue: A2's whatCountsAsHeld may be broader than anyone has been applying, and if read literally it creates a trap.
forTheCaptain.detail: A2 lists 'the compiled state profile for the family's jurisdiction' UNCONDITIONALLY, as a separate bullet from 'any record the route obligation census names as a requiredSourceId for this route'. Read literally, CA-california.json is a held source for all seven California families, not just ca-prop64-set whose census actually binds it. That profile holds '1203.4 dismissal petition ~$60-$150 per case; County-set; some counties charge no fee for 1203.4'. But §1203.4 is NOT §1203.41, §1203.42, §1203.43, §1203.4a or §17(b) — publishing that figure on those five would be 'a rule inferred from a neighbouring jurisdiction or a sibling route', which A2's own whatDoesNotCount forbids. The two limbs of A2 point opposite ways here.

forTheCaptain.captainDecision: Whether the unconditional compiled-profile limb binds a family whose census does not name the profile, and — separately — how a repair should treat a profile fact that is real for a sibling statute but not for this route. This worker's reading is that the manifests are right and 'do not publish a figure' must be respected for those five, but that is a reading, not a ruling.
